title: Ultrafast Density Gradient Accumulation in 3D Analytical Placement with Divergence Theorem
problem: Density gradient accumulation is a critical bottleneck in 3D analytical placement, especially for mixed-size designs with large macros; 3D placement requires larger grids than 2D, exacerbating the computational burden.
motivation: 3D placement for advanced packaging is increasingly important; reducing this bottleneck directly improves design automation tool efficiency and enables faster design iteration.
method: Algorithm inspired by divergence theorem reduces density gradient accumulation time complexity. Implementations provided for both CPU and GPU to leverage diverse hardware capabilities efficiently.
key_novelty: Divergence theorem-based algorithm reducing time complexity of density gradient accumulation in 3D placement.
contributions: Novel algorithm reducing density gradient complexity via divergence theorem
limitations: Comparison limited to single 3D placer baseline; applicability to 2D placement not discussed; algorithm details sparse from abstract.
